core.title: Bind interlocking trace assertions to the declared route
core.given: An e2e test (a file of the e2e test role) in an interlocking context
core.when: it references or inspects the runtime trace of an interlocking execution — the trace recorded on the execution's result — with or without assertions
core.then: Assert every required trace field — interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, routeCategory, guardId, resolutionStrategy, resolutionReason (the domain field names; each stack recognises its own rendering of them) — binding the executed route to the interlocking declaration artifact the run came from (an artifact of the stack's declared plan-artifact kind) and to its resolution outcome.
prefer: Extend the flagged trace assertion so the captured trace is checked for all required trace fields.
Assert the values against the interlocking declaration artifact the run came from (the stack's declared plan-artifact kind).
avoid: Checking only one field (e.g. only the selected train id): a run on a different route, category, or guard would still match.
Naming required fields only in comments; comment content is masked by the check.
unless: The test never references the runtime trace object.
The test is not in an interlocking context (no interlocking route, train, interlocking, or runner reference).
The file is outside the realizing stack's scope: renderings of this convention in other stacks are owned by those stacks' own realizations.
core.why: The runtime trace of an interlocking execution proves which declared route actually executed; a trace test that does not bind the declared route lets execution drift from declaration silently and undetected.
evidence: Every e2e test in an interlocking context that references the runtime trace contains assertions on all required trace fields (interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, routeCategory, guardId, resolutionStrategy, resolutionReason).
The realizing stack's convention check reports zero violations for this rule.
verification: Scope: e2e tests of the realizing stack, in the stack's declared test languages, that are in an interlocking context; which per-stack discovery applies (where the stack's e2e tests live, and how a trace reference and the field assertions are recognised) is delegated to each stack's realization.
A file is a trace-binding test when it references the runtime trace in an interlocking context; for such a test every required trace field must be asserted.
Comment content is masked before the field search; a required field named only in a comment does not count.
Any missing required field is a violation listing the gap (the missing fields).
Severity 1, disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode.

values: test references the runtime trace of an interlocking execution in an interlocking context, with or without existing assertions

fires: An e2e test in an interlocking context asserts on the runtime trace but checks only one field (e.g. only the selected train id).
An interlocking e2e test references or inspects the runtime trace without any assertions yet, omitting required fields such as the guard id or the resolution reason.
doesNotFire: An interlocking e2e test that never references the runtime trace object.
An e2e test with no interlocking context, even if it uses a variable named like the trace.
A rendering of an interlocking trace test in another stack, owned by that stack's own realization.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack's e2e test files live; the realization scans only these files for interlocking trace references and required-field assertions.

The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role; the interlocking declaration that a trace-binding test must bind its asserted values to is an artifact of this kind (for Bun, the interlocking YAML declaration).
The languages of the stack's test files; scopes this test-side check to the realizing stack's e2e tests, independently of the production-source languages (proposed key; see proposedKeys).

proposedKeys.meaning: The languages of the stack's test files (unit, acceptance, e2e); scopes test-side convention checks and test discovery to the realizing stack's tests.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: tooling.languages lists only the languages of production source, which need not coincide with the languages of test files; test-side discovery (e.g. which e2e files this rule scans) needs its own key rather than misusing the production-language key.

bunOnly.text: Content-level scan of the test file (comments masked) for a bare `trace` identifier plus interlocking context (route/train/interlocking token or runner symbol); provided by the bun_interlocking_coverage detector family. Any reference counts, with or without existing assertions.
bunOnly.reason: The concrete token heuristic (bare `trace` identifier, interlocking route/train/interlocking token or runner symbol) and the detector family name are per-stack discovery, which the Bun text itself delegates to the realization; the core states the finding neutrally.

bunOnly.text: Detector: JS validator `tester.bun.interlocking-trace-binds-declared-route`, member of the `bun_interlocking_coverage` FAMILY; scans each interlocking-related test in the consumer's `e2e/**/*.ts`.
bunOnly.reason: Detector, validator and family ids of this one rule are realization details; the core's verification names the check generically and takes the scan location from the profile (roles.e2e_test.path).

bunOnly.text: A file is a trace-binding test when it references a bare `trace` identifier in an interlocking context (any interlocking route/train/interlocking token or runner symbol); for such a file every required field token must appear.
bunOnly.reason: The neutral definition (runtime-trace reference in an interlocking context, all required fields asserted) is in core verification; the token-level recognition heuristic is delegated per-stack discovery.

bunOnly.text: Required field tokens (TS camelCase): interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, routeCategory, guardId, resolutionStrategy, resolutionReason.
bunOnly.reason: The camelCase token spelling is the TypeScript rendering of the domain field names; the core names the domain fields and each stack's check recognises its own rendering.

bunOnly.text: The bun_interlocking_coverage-family JS detector reports zero RAW violations for this rule.
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun realization's concrete detector family; the neutral evidence is that the realizing stack's convention check reports zero violations.

classification.note: 'Bun e2e test (e2e/**/*.ts)' neutralizes to the e2e test role; the concrete location comes from the profile.

'bare `trace` identifier ... on an interlocking execution's TrainResult' neutralizes to referencing the runtime trace of an interlocking execution; the identifier-level heuristic stays in the realization.

The seven required trace fields are domain field names and are kept. 'its interlocking YAML declaration' neutralizes to 'the interlocking declaration artifact the run came from (an artifact of the stack's declared plan-artifact kind)'; the declaration's concrete kind — YAML for Bun — is profile data via roles.plan_artifact.kinds, so instantiation restores the YAML binding exactly.
'TrainResult trace' neutralizes to 'the runtime trace of an interlocking execution'; the reasoning is domain-level and unchanged.
'all seven fields (TS camelCase)' neutralizes to 'all required trace fields'; the casing detail is realization-specific and captured under verifier_detail[2].
'the interlocking YAML declaration' neutralizes to the interlocking declaration artifact of the stack's plan-artifact kind; the YAML kind is restored on instantiation via roles.plan_artifact.kinds.
Neutral example: 'only the selected train id' instead of the concrete field token; the drift argument is unchanged.
Comment masking is generic checker behaviour, not stack-specific; restated neutrally in both the core avoid list and verification, restricted to comments exactly as the Bun checker does.
Already neutral: no runtime trace reference, no obligation.
'route/train/interlocking token or runner symbol' neutralizes to 'interlocking route, train, interlocking, or runner reference'.
'The stack is not Bun (owned by its own workspace package)' neutralizes to per-stack ownership of realizations; no stack is named, and the exception is preserved.
'e2e/**/*.ts file referencing a bare `trace` identifier' neutralizes to 'e2e test in an interlocking context that references the runtime trace'; the required field names are domain names.
Neutral counterpart: the realizing stack's convention check reports zero violations; the concrete detector family is Bun-only.
Generic scope ('scans interlocking e2e tests of the realizing stack') is in core verification; detector/validator/family ids and the concrete path are realization details.
The trace-binding-test definition is in core verification; the bare-identifier token heuristic is realization detail.
The neutral content (every required trace field must be asserted) is covered by core then and verification; only the TS-camelCase token spelling is Bun-only.
Comment masking is a generic check mechanism, restated neutrally; masking covers comments only, exactly as the Bun checker does (no prose exclusion).
'RAW violation listing the gap' neutralizes to 'a violation listing the gap (the missing fields)'.
The deference of per-stack discovery to the realization is kept verbatim in spirit in core verification.
Per-rule severity and disposition are core verification, not profile keys: severity 1, strict disposition, fails on every finding.
The path glob is profile data; in the core it becomes the file_kind fact for the e2e_test role.
file_kind e2e_test is already role-level and is kept as the core's file_kind fact.

The language of the scanned test files is stack data that scopes test discovery; no existing vocabulary key covers it (tooling.languages is production source only, and misusing it would conflate the two), so the key tooling.test_languages is proposed. The core's verification scope references the stack's declared test languages, and per-stack ownership lives in core unless[2].
Task terms are domain words (interlocking, trace, route, TrainResult), kept unchanged as a non-gating hint; the rule fires on the finding regardless of task wording.
The finding ('test references the runtime trace in an interlocking context') is neutral; the token heuristic and detector family that provide the observer are realization details.

neutralityNotes: The seven required trace fields are named in the core by their domain names (interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, routeCategory, guardId, resolutionStrategy, resolutionReason); the concrete token spelling (TS camelCase) and the bare-`trace`-identifier detection heuristic could not be made neutral, but bun.json itself delegates per-stack discovery to the realization, so the core keeps that deference in verification and needs no profile key for it. The declaration artifact is kept neutral by referencing the stack's declared plan-artifact kind: 'interlocking YAML declaration' is restored on instantiation via roles.plan_artifact.kinds, so the core neither names a format nor weakens the binding. The language filter of the scanned tests could not use an existing key (tooling.languages is production-source only), so tooling.test_languages is proposed and used as profile data. Masking in the check covers comments only, matching the Bun checker exactly. unless[2]'s 'the stack is not Bun' is preserved as a neutral per-stack-ownership exception. Per-rule severity (1) and disposition (strict) stay in core verification, not in the profile.
